chapter: Club Alabam and the Europe contract
title: J. Rosamund Johnson's advice to listen to the bad bands
summary: The composer Rosamund Johnson, passed over for the Europe job, tells Wooding to listen to the bad bands to learn what not to do.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: tape anytime. When I got the chance to go to Europe -- I'm a little ahead of my story, but I'll come back. When I got a chance to go to Europe, there was a great man -- which I considered a great man. Rosamund Johnson, a great Negro composer and a student of music, see. And he's written a lot of spirituals, I mean he's edited a lot of spirituals and had some folk songs of his own, I mean, art songs of his own.
So he tried for the job but he didn't have any chance to get it anyhow, because my manager had it, you see. Even though I wasn't no musician compared to Rosamund Johnson in those days.

So, anyhow, but he come to me afterwards, he was leaving. I met him coming in the place. I was coming in the place and he was going out. He said, "Well, Sam, I see you have got this job." Now get these words he said. He said, "Now, you're going to Europe. My advice to you is to watch all the bad bands, listen closely to all the bad bands that you'll hear. Then you'll know what not to do." And he said, "Well good luck to you." I thought he was joking, that'll show you how dizzy I was. And I thought he was joking, and I started laughing, "Yeah that's right." And it suddenly hit me that this man had said

something great. And I turned around to thank him -- next time I saw him he was dead. But I've never had a chance to thank him for that statement that has been with me and should be with all young musicians. In fact, any line you're in. Don't worry about those that are good. Worry about the bad ones. It's a negative approach, but it's a darned good approach for any youngster coming up in the business. Look for the things that are not right. Then you can say, "Well I'm glad that I saw that. Now I will know not to do that." Well that was one of the successes.
